title: Gafgyt_Botnet_Investigation_893
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Gafgyt (BASHLITE) botnet infection on a Linux-based system. Gafgyt is known to compromise IoT devices and Linux systems, often conducting DDoS attacks. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the botnet activity.
outcomes: Identify unauthorized or suspicious services responsible for periodic external communication.
Investigate network connections to identify command-and-control (C2) servers.
Analyze network traffic to determine the target of malicious activities.
Collect forensic evidence supporting the identified botnet activity.
Apply appropriate network controls to mitigate the attack.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Gafgyt (BASHLITE) botnet infection on a Linux-based system. Gafgyt is known to compromise IoT devices and Linux systems, often conducting DDoS attacks. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the botnet activity.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the sandbox via the provided cloud environment. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from `bot1`. Your task is to identify the service responsible for this suspicious behavior. The service name is the timer flag `bot-beacon-busybox.timer`.
levels.solution: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers and look for the flag `bot-beacon-busybox.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and their network activity. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers.

levels.title: Determine C2 Server
levels.content: Now that you have identified the suspicious service, your next step is to determine the external command-and-control (C2) server it is communicating with. The C2 IP address is the IP flag `192.168.70.5`.
levels.solution: Use the command `cat /usr/local/lib/.botcache/beacon.sh` to view the beacon script and identify the flag `192.168.70.5`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Inspect the service configuration and network connections. Use the command `cat /usr/local/lib/.botcache/beacon.sh` to view the beacon script.

levels.title: Identify Target System
levels.content: The suspicious service is generating a high volume of network traffic. Identify the target system of this traffic. The victim IP address is the IP flag `192.168.80.100`.
levels.solution: Use the command `cat /usr/local/lib/.botcache/flood.sh` to view the flood script and identify the flag `192.168.80.100`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Analyze the network flows and service logs. Use the command `cat /usr/local/lib/.botcache/flood.sh` to view the flood script.
